The build, the tests still in the suite (137 passed), fmt, slither and artifacts all exit 0; six test files are parked as .todo for the porters.

What changed:
- **Auction base**: `src/auction/ERC20EnglishAuction.sol` is now `src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol`, contract `EnglishAuction` (git mv). `paymentToken`, the IERC20/IERC20Metadata/SafeERC20 imports, every token branch, the decimals logic, `UnsupportedTokenBehavior` and `AuctionConfig.paymentToken` are removed. `_isNewWinningBid` is untouched and `verify-upstream` still passes.
- **One unit name**: I removed `tokenUnit()` and kept only `SYMBOL_PRICE`. The site (`site/chain.js`, `site/abi.js`) still reads `tokenUnit()` and must switch.
- **KilimAuction**: `Config.paymentToken`, `deliverSymbols`, `deliverTo`, `symbolsPending`, the delivery queue, `deliveryCursor`, the `DELIVERY_*` constants, `DeliveryFailed` and the `reentrancy-no-eth` suppression are removed. `bid`, `claimSymbols`, credit ranges, `settle`, the prize self-call and both gas floors are unchanged.
- **Kilim.sol and src/render**: no change needed; nothing there mentioned tokens as payment.
- **Deploy script and configs**: the token and decimals fields, constants, checks and print lines are removed from `script/DeployKilim.s.sol` and the three `deploy/*.json` files. The other chain-1 pins are unchanged. `deploy/local.json` now uses a 0.01 ETH reserve.
- **Tests**: `test/mocks/MockUSD.sol` and `test/Delivery.t.sol` are deleted. `TestBase.sol` has `config()` without a token, `UNIT = 0.001 ether`, `RESERVE`, and the helpers listed in api_notes. I ported NativeRegistration, SponsoredRegistration and GasFloors, plus the two render tests that used the token mock.
- **Provenance**: `vendor/thirdweb/manifest.json` points at the new path; `vendor/thirdweb/NOTICE` and `REUSE.md` are reworded for the ETH design with attribution kept. The `package.json` description no longer says "stablecoin".

Contract sizes after the change:

| Contract | Runtime (bytes) | Initcode (bytes) | Runtime before |
|---|---|---|---|
| KilimAuction | 10,967 | 30,349 | 13,567 |
| Kilim | 15,314 | 17,031 | 15,314 |

Two things I changed beyond a pure removal, both outside the on-chain behaviour:
- **Deploy script reserve guard**: the generic "reserve price" refusal now requires exactly 0.01 ETH on every chain, matching the constructor. Before, it only required a whole multiple of 0.001 ETH and the constructor rejected the rest.
- **Constructor check**: the reserve checks collapse into one `reservePrice != REGISTRATION_BALANCE` condition with the same `InvalidConfiguration` error. The dropped checks (zero, whole unit, uint128) were already implied by it.

Nothing was deployed, broadcast, committed or pushed. The renames and deletions are staged in the index because of `git mv` / `git rm`.

contracts.api_notes:
NEW NAMES
- File: src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol, contract `EnglishAuction` (was ERC20EnglishAuction). Import: `import {EnglishAuction} from "../src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol";`. Errors are `EnglishAuction.X.selector`.
- Bid unit: `SYMBOL_PRICE` (public constant, 0.001 ether) is the only name. `tokenUnit()` is removed.
- `KilimAuction.Config` has 14 fields, in order: treasury, collectionOwner, startsAt, duration, extensionWindow, incrementBps, reservePrice, symbolCap, maxSymbolsPerBid, motifCount, maxCells, geometryHash, rendererHash, renderer. `EnglishAuction.AuctionConfig`: treasury, startsAt, duration, extensionWindow, incrementBps, reservePrice.
- The constructor reverts `InvalidConfiguration` unless `reservePrice == REGISTRATION_BALANCE` (0.01 ether). There is no other valid reserve on any chain.

REMOVED FROM THE ABI
- Functions: `paymentToken()`, `tokenUnit()`, `deliverSymbols(uint256)`, `deliverTo(address,uint256)`, `symbolsPending()`, `deliveryCursor()`, `DELIVERY_BATCH()`.
- Errors: `UnsupportedTokenBehavior`, and `SafeERC20FailedOperation` (it came in with the SafeERC20 import).
- Event: `DeliveryFailed`.
- `symbolsPending()` equals `symbolsAllocated() - symbolsClaimed()`; both getters remain.

UNCHANGED (same signatures and behaviour)
- `bid(uint256 amount, uint256 minimumReward, uint256 expectedFirstSymbolId)` payable, `msg.value == amount` or `IncorrectPayment`.
- `register()`, `registerFor(wallet, deadline, signature)`, `registrationDigest`, `registered`, `registrationCount`, `REGISTRATION_TARGET` (100), `REGISTRATION_BALANCE`.
- `minimumBid`, `rewardForBid`, `claimSymbols(quantity, to)`, `unclaimedSymbolRanges`, `symbolCredits`, `symbolsAllocated`, `symbolsClaimed`.
- `settle`, `deliverPrize` (self-call only), `claimPrize(to)`, `prizeClaimed`, `withdrawRefund(to)`, `refunds`, `refundLiability`, `payOutbidRefund` (self-call only), `withdrawProceeds(to)`, `proceedsDue`, `liabilities`.
- Errors `InsufficientGas`, `EthTransferFailed`, `RegistrationIncomplete`, `RegistrationClosed`, `TreasuryCannotBid`, `NonWholeUnitBid`, `BidTooLow(minimum)` and the rest.
- Events `BidPlaced`, `SymbolsClaimed`, `PrizeClaimed`, `PrizeDeliveryFailed`, `RefundPaid`, `RefundDeferred`, `RefundWithdrawn`, `Registered`, `AuctionStarted`, `AuctionSettled`, `ProceedsWithdrawn`.
- Gas constants: REFUND_GAS 150,000 with floor `REFUND_GAS + REFUND_GAS/63 + 60_000`; PRIZE_GAS 500,000 with floor `PRIZE_GAS + PRIZE_GAS/63 + 50_000`.
- The auction has no receive or fallback: plain ETH transfers and unknown selectors revert.

DEPLOY SCRIPT (script/DeployKilim.s.sol)
- Removed: `interface IERC20Decimals`, `LAUNCH_PAYMENT_TOKEN`, `LAUNCH_TOKEN_DECIMALS`, `Config.tokenDecimals`, the JSON keys `.auction.paymentToken` and `.auction.tokenDecimals`, and the refusals "token decimals", "payment token has no code", "mainnet launch value: paymentToken", "mainnet launch value: tokenDecimals".
- Kept: every other `LAUNCH_*` constant and refusal string. "reserve price" now fires when `reservePrice != LAUNCH_RESERVE_PRICE` (0.01 ether) on any chain; on chain 1 "mainnet launch value: reservePrice" still fires first.
- deploy/*.json: the `auction` object no longer has `paymentToken` or `tokenDecimals`.

TESTBASE (test/TestBase.sol)
- `uint256 UNIT = 0.001 ether` (one symbol per UNIT), `uint256 RESERVE = 0.01 ether` (10 UNIT), `uint160 REGISTRANT_BASE = 0x5EED0000`.
- `config()` takes no argument. Defaults: treasury TREASURY, collectionOwner PAGE_OWNER, startsAt now + 1 hours, duration 22 hours, extensionWindow 10 minutes, incrementBps 500, reservePrice RESERVE, symbolCap 10000, maxSymbolsPerBid 1000, motifCount 812, maxCells 256, mock renderer.
- The default reserve was 25 * UNIT before. It must now be RESERVE, so an opening bid earns 10 symbols, and with 500 bps the next minimum after 0.01 ETH is 0.011 ETH (rounded up to a whole UNIT).
- `registrant(uint256 i) returns (address)`: the i-th throwaway wallet.
- `_registerWallets(KilimAuction auction, uint256 count)`: registers `count` more throwaway wallets, each dealt exactly 0.01 ETH. Needs `block.timestamp >= startsAt`. Repeatable; continues from `registrationCount()`.
- `_openBidding(KilimAuction auction)`: warps to startsAt if it is still ahead, then fills the remaining slots to 100. No bid is placed and `endsAt` stays 0.
- `_fund(address who, uint256 amount)`: `vm.deal`; sets the balance, does not add.
- `_bid(KilimAuction auction, address bidder, uint256 amount)`: pranks and calls `bid{value: amount}(amount, 0, 0)`. It reads nothing first, so it can follow `vm.expectRevert` directly.
- `_registerWallets` and `_openBidding` read views first: do not put them directly after `vm.prank` or `vm.expectRevert`.
- A test contract may keep its own private `_bid(address,uint256)` or `_fund(address)`; the different parameter lists overload cleanly.

Example:
    KilimAuction auction = new KilimAuction(config());
    _openBidding(auction);
    _fund(ALICE, 1 ether); _fund(BOB, 1 ether);
    _bid(auction, ALICE, RESERVE);          // 10 credits, clock starts
    _bid(auction, BOB, 11 * UNIT);          // ALICE is refunded inside this bid
    vm.prank(ALICE); auction.claimSymbols(10, ALICE);
    vm.warp(auction.endsAt()); auction.settle();   // the 1/1 goes to BOB
    vm.prank(TREASURY); auction.withdrawProceeds(TREASURY);
For 99-then-1 tests: `vm.warp(auction.startsAt()); _registerWallets(auction, 99);` then register the 100th wallet yourself.

- `testSymbolsAreMintedOnlyByClaim`: no bid, refund or settlement mints symbols.

- Bid amounts are the same numbers as before (25, 27, 29, ...), now in units of 0.001 ETH, so symbol IDs and credit counts are unchanged.

  - `configure(bool rejecting, bool burning)`: rejecting makes `receive()` revert, which forces a deferred refund or `EthTransferFailed`; burning makes `receive()` burn all its gas.
  - `hook(address target, uint256 value, bytes payload)`: a callback with ETH attached, run from both `receive()` and `onERC721Received`; the result is in `callbackSucceeded()`.
  - `fire()`: makes the same call from outside any callback and returns whether it succeeded.
  - Fund it with `vm.deal` and bid with `vm.prank(address(bidder))`.
- `mocks/Receiver.sol` and `mocks/RangeInspector.sol` have no receive function, so an ETH refund to them is always deferred. Their `execute()` is not payable, so bid for them with `vm.prank` plus `bid{value: ...}`, not through `execute`.
- In `KilimAuctionTest` the private helpers are `_bid(address user, uint256 units)` (units of 0.001 ETH), `_fund(address)` (1e30 wei), `_bidMinimum(address)`, `_assertSolvent()` and `_rejectingBidder()`. They overload the TestBase helpers without conflict.

On a real chain that state cannot occur: registration cannot fill before startsAt, so a pre-start bid always reverts RegistrationIncomplete first. The test now asserts that too, on a fresh auction. The `block.timestamp < startsAt` clause in _handleBid is therefore unreachable in practice. I did not change it; it is a candidate for removal if the artist wants less code.

testForcedEthDoesNotAlterLiabilitiesOrRewards documents that ETH forced into the auction (selfdestruct or a block reward) stays there forever: no function pays it out. The old suite showed the same for donated tokens.

No test was deleted. The details that changed:

- **ReuseRegression**:
  - The blacklist test now uses a wallet that rejects ETH, and also checks that pulling the refund back to that wallet fails and keeps it.
  - The accidental-ETH test became `testMismatchedValueRevertsWithoutTakingBid`: over-, under- and zero-value bids revert with `IncorrectPayment`.
  - New `testMismatchedOutbidLeavesTheLeaderInPlace` covers a wrong-value bid against a standing leader.
  - The direct-payment test also sends ETH with an unknown selector.
  - The quote fuzz lost its decimals parameter, because the unit is now fixed at 0.001 ETH.
  - The oversized-bid test adds a fully paid bid one wei past the uint128 bound.
- **LaunchConfig**:
  - The reserve is 0.01 ETH and the fixture registers 100 wallets.
  - The 10% ladder is now 10, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 21, 24, 27, 30, 33, 37, 41, then 46 thousandths.
  - `testOneDollarIsOneSymbolWithNoPerBidCap` is renamed `testOneUnitIsOneSymbolWithNoPerBidCap`.
- **Lifecycle**: same flow with bids of 0.01 and 0.011 ETH, so the totals are 21 symbols allocated, claimed and minted instead of 52.
- **AuctionInvariants**:
  - The three actors are wallets that can reject ETH, burn gas or refuse NFTs, which replaces the blacklist toggle.
  - The `deliver` handler action is gone because `deliverSymbols` no longer exists.
  - `donate` forces ETH in with `vm.deal`.
  - The handler measures every payout by the recipient's balance change.
  - The escrow invariant adds three checks: balance >= liabilities, deposits == refunds + proceeds + liabilities, and the three wallets hold exactly what the ledger says.
  - New `testHandlerReachesDeferredRefundAndPrizeFallback` shows the handler does reach a deferred refund and the `claimPrize` fallback.

Every bid, settle and withdraw step in the ported files now asserts `address(auction).balance == liabilities()` (ReuseRegression, Lifecycle, LaunchConfig bids).

EIP-8037 (State Creation Gas Cost Increase) is in Last Call with a deadline of 1 November 2026 and is part of the Glamsterdam work (execution-spec tests exist under amsterdam/eip8037; client docs fix cost_per_state_byte at 1530 for Glamsterdam; press reports put mainnet activation in late 2026, date not final). findings.description: The floor makes a bid's gas need jump with state. The opening bid has no refund and no floor; any later bid must reach the refund with about 212,000 gas. findings.description: Design note behind the first finding. Both try/catch blocks treat any failure of the self-call as the receiver's fault. For the refund that is harmless: the only other causes are infeasible (call depth) and the bidder keeps a pull refund. For the prize it is not harmless, because a cause outside the winner's control exists (Kilim's guard, first finding) and the fallback is winner-only. deliverPrize also has no settled check of its own (F-21, known). Nothing here loses ETH.

Every statement in the note holds against the ETH-only code on disk.

1. Bare catches. EnglishAuction._refundOutbid (src/auction/EnglishAuction.sol:237-243) and KilimAuction._afterSettle (src/KilimAuction.sol:196-199) both use `catch { ... }` with no reason captured or emitted. RefundDeferred(bidder, amount) and PrizeDeliveryFailed(winner) carry no cause.

2. No third-party retry. After a failed refund only the bidder can pull it: withdrawRefund reads refunds[msg.sender], and payOutbidRefund is self-only. After a failed delivery settle() reverts AlreadySettled, deliverPrize is self-only, and claimPrize requires msg.sender == highestBidder (src/KilimAuction.sol:213-217).

3. A cause outside the winner's control exists, and I reproduced it. Kilim.mintMasterpiece is `onlyMinter nonReentrant` (src/Kilim.sol:263). Kilim.weave is nonReentrant and calls _safeMint(msg.sender, ...) (src/Kilim.sol:285). Any holder of four symbols who is not the winner can call weave from a contract and call auction.settle() from its onERC721Received. A winner that can hold an NFT but cannot call claimPrize (the PoolWinner shape in test/GasFloors.t.sol) then never receives the 1/1. The control test shows a plain settle() delivers to the same winner.

4. deliverPrize has no settled check of its own (src/KilimAuction.sol:203-209). It is reachable only from _afterSettle, so this is not exploitable; it is AUDIT.md F-21 as stated.

5. Nothing loses ETH: in the PoC the treasury withdraws the full proceeds and the auction balance ends at zero. A deferred refund stays owed to its bidder.
